fixed.q: In order to move objects in computer graphics that generate animation effects, which of the following is necessary?
fixed.w: Animation moves objects through successive transformations (translation, rotation, scaling).

fixed.q: ______ and ______ views cannot be framed together for rendering a computer visual appropriately.
fixed.w: Orthogonal projection and horizontal view cannot be framed together.

fixed.q: Which of the following displays uses an electron beam that operates like a pencil to create a line image on the CRT screen?
fixed.w: Random-scan (vector) displays move the beam like a pencil to draw lines directly.

fixed.q: Which of the following curves is particularly a kind of spline generated from a set of control points by forming a set of polynomial functions with reference to computer graphics?
fixed.w: A Bézier curve is a parametric curve defined by a set of control points through Bernstein polynomials.

fixed.q: In the Cohen–Sutherland line clipping algorithm, if a line ______ the clipping window, then the line is required to be clipped as it is considered partially visible.
fixed.w: In Cohen–Sutherland, a line that intersects the clipping window is partially visible and must be clipped.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a clipping algorithm?
fixed.w: Liang–Barsky is a line-clipping algorithm; DDA, Bresenham and mid-point are drawing algorithms.

fixed.q: Which of these is NOT a parameter upon which the influence of lighting is based?
fixed.w: Illumination depends on the light source, the surface and the observer's position, not on the rendering algorithm.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about the Z-buffer algorithm in computer graphics? i) It is an image space method to detect visible surface. ii) In this method, a depth buffer is used to store the depth values of each position and a refresh (frame) buffer is used to store the intensity values or colour values for each position. iii) In this method, object edges can be anti-aliased. iv) This method can only find one visible surface at each pixel position.
fixed.w: A plain Z-buffer cannot anti-alias edges, so iii is incorrect; i, ii and iv are true (iv is a real limitation).

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) The clipping process divides each element into a visible and an invisible portion; the visible portion is selected and the invisible portion is discarded. ii) Clipping can be applied through hardware as well as software. iii) Point clipping, area clipping and text clipping are types of clipping.
fixed.w: All three clipping statements are true.

fixed.q: Solid modelling is based on ______, ______ and ______ geometric representation of a physical object.
fixed.w: A solid model must be a complete, valid and unambiguous representation.

fixed.q: When a plane is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on that plane is a/an ______.
fixed.w: A plane perpendicular to the reference plane projects onto it as a straight line.

fixed.q: Which of the following does the actual display in a computer?
fixed.w: CRT. The display device (CRT/monitor) produces the actual display.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are interpolation methods in computer graphics? i) Inverse Distance Weighted ii) Kriging iii) Natural Neighbor iv) Spline v) Topo to raster vi) Compiler
o: i, ii, iii, iv and v only
i, ii, iii, iv, v and vi
fixed.w: IDW, kriging, natural neighbour, spline and topo-to-raster are interpolation methods; a compiler is not.

fixed.q: Circle have ______ way symmetry.
fixed.w: A circle has eight-way symmetry (octants), which the midpoint and Bresenham circle algorithms use.

fixed.q: What is the full form of JPEG image forms?
fixed.w: JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group.

fixed.q: The maximum number of points that can be displayed without overlap on a CRT is referred to as ______.
fixed.w: Resolution is the maximum number of points that can be shown on a CRT without overlap.

fixed.q: Random scan monitors are also referred to as
fixed.w: Random-scan displays are also called vector, stroke-writing or calligraphic displays.

fixed.q: The refresh rate below which the picture flickers is
fixed.w: Below about 25 frames per second the picture visibly flickers.

fixed.q: ______ is a line drawing algorithm based only on integer calculation.
o: Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) line drawing algorithm
fixed.w: Bresenham's algorithm uses only integer arithmetic; DDA uses floating point.

fixed.q: What is the name of the .NET collection class that enables an element to be accessed using a unique key?
fixed.w: Hashtable stores key–value pairs, so elements are accessed by a unique key.

fixed.q: The technology of .NET is developed by ______ and was launched in ______.
fixed.w: Microsoft launched the .NET Framework in 2002.

fixed.q: Which of the following is an action or occurrence such as a mouse click, a key press, mouse movements or any system-generated notification in ASP.NET?
fixed.w: An event is an action such as a click, key press or system notification that ASP.NET code responds to.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a Microsoft ActiveX control that will sort through a data file, extrapolate the necessary information and produce that information in specified areas on the web page?
fixed.w: The Tabular Data Control (TDC) ActiveX control reads a delimited data file and displays the data in specified areas of a web page.

fixed.q: Which of the following controls in VB.NET is used to select one option from a number of choices?
fixed.w: A RadioButton lets the user pick one option from a group.

fixed.q: Which of the following is FALSE with reference to a constructor in C#.NET?
o: It can have a return type.
All classes have constructors by default.
Constructor name must match the class name.
The constructor is called when the object is created.
fixed.w: A C# constructor never has a return type, not even void, so A is false.

fixed.q: How to write the dot net server control?
fixed.w: ASP.NET server controls need runat="server".

fixed.q: ______ is a code that consists of a CPU- and platform-independent set of instructions, which can be easily converted to the native code.
fixed.w: MSIL (CIL) is CPU-independent intermediate code that the JIT compiles into native code.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the execution engine for .NET applications and serves as the interface between .NET applications and the operating system?
fixed.w: The CLR is .NET's execution engine.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of ADO.NET?
fixed.w: ADO.NET features include interoperability, maintainability, programmability, performance and scalability; 'reachability' is not one.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) VB.NET is an object-oriented programming language implemented in the .NET Framework. ii) VB.NET is a subset of Visual Basic 6.0. iii) .NET is a free, cross-platform, open-source developer platform for building many different types of applications.
fixed.w: VB.NET is object-oriented on .NET and .NET is free, cross-platform and open source, but VB.NET is not a subset of VB6.

fixed.q: Which of the following languages is a non-.NET language?
fixed.w: C#, F# and J# are .NET languages; standard Pascal is not.

fixed.q: What is the full form of WPF with respect to ASP.NET?
fixed.w: WPF = Windows Presentation Foundation.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) The Just-In-Time compiler (JIT) is a part of the Common Language Runtime (CLR). ii) .NET Framework is part of the .NET platform, a collection of technologies for building apps for Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android. iii) ASP.NET applications are compiled codes, written using the extensible and reusable components or objects present in the .NET framework.
fixed.w: The JIT is part of the CLR, .NET spans many platforms, and ASP.NET apps are compiled. All true.

fixed.q: The term ______ in ASP.NET means that data that is collected from a source is bound to the controls that provide the read and write connection to the data.
fixed.w: Data binding connects data sources to controls.

fixed.q: What is the description of append keyword of Visual Basic .NET keyword?
o: Used as a symbolic constant in the file open function
fixed.w: In VB.NET, Append is used as a symbolic constant in the FileOpen function (OpenMode.Append).

fixed.q: What is AJAX in ASP.NET?
fixed.w: AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML.

fixed.q: In ASP.NET, the difference between Response.Write() and Response.Output.Write() is
fixed.w: Response.Output.Write() supports formatted output, like String.Format.

fixed.q: Where is the default session data stored in ASP.NET?
fixed.w: ASP.NET's default session mode is InProc (in-process).

fixed.q: In ASP.NET, which namespace provides forms authentication?
fixed.w: Forms authentication is in System.Web.Security.

fixed.q: In ASP.NET, what is Global.asax used for?
o: To implement application and session level events
fixed.w: Global.asax handles application- and session-level events.

fixed.q: Bresenham's line algorithm is preferred over DDA because it:
fixed.w: Bresenham uses integer increments and a decision parameter. DDA uses floating-point additions and rounding.

fixed.q: In the Cohen–Sutherland line-clipping algorithm, each region code has:
fixed.w: Each endpoint gets a 4-bit outcode (top, bottom, right, left).

fixed.q: The Sutherland–Hodgman algorithm is used for:
fixed.w: Sutherland–Hodgman clips a polygon against each edge of the clip window in turn.

fixed.q: Homogeneous coordinates are used in 2-D graphics so that:
o: Translation can be done by matrix multiplication
fixed.w: Using 3×3 matrices, translation, rotation and scaling can all be combined by multiplication.

fixed.q: The Z-buffer (depth buffer) algorithm is used for:
fixed.w: For each pixel, the Z-buffer keeps the depth of the nearest surface drawn so far.

fixed.q: A Bezier curve of degree n has how many control points?
fixed.w: A Bezier curve of degree n uses n + 1 control points and passes through the first and last ones.

fixed.q: Projection in which parallel lines converge at a vanishing point is:
fixed.w: Perspective projection makes distant objects look smaller. Parallel projections (orthographic, oblique) keep lines parallel.

fixed.q: The colour model used by printers is:
fixed.w: Printers use subtractive CMY(K). Monitors use additive RGB.

fixed.q: The memory that holds the intensity values of all pixels for the screen is the:
fixed.w: The frame (refresh) buffer stores pixel values. Size = resolution × bits per pixel.

fixed.q: In .NET, the runtime environment that manages execution of code is the:
fixed.w: The CLR provides JIT compilation, garbage collection, memory management and security.

fixed.q: .NET source code is first compiled into:
fixed.w: Compilers produce MSIL/CIL; the JIT compiler in the CLR turns it into native code at run time.

fixed.q: The set of rules that .NET languages must follow to interoperate is the:
fixed.w: The CLS is a subset of the CTS that all .NET languages support, so they can work together.

fixed.q: Shared assemblies used by many applications are stored in the:
fixed.w: The GAC stores strong-named shared assemblies.

fixed.q: In ASP.NET, the mechanism that keeps page and control values between postbacks is:
fixed.w: ViewState stores state in a hidden field on the page.

fixed.q: In ADO.NET, the object that works in disconnected mode is the:
fixed.w: The DataSet is an in-memory, disconnected cache of data. The DataReader is forward-only and read-only in connected mode.

fixed.q: In the DDA line algorithm with slope |m| ≤ 1, x is incremented by 1 and y by:
fixed.w: For |m| ≤ 1, step in x by 1 and add m to y. For |m| > 1, step in y by 1 and add 1/m to x.

fixed.q: The midpoint circle algorithm exploits the circle's:
fixed.w: Computing one octant gives the other seven points by symmetry: (±x, ±y), (±y, ±x).

fixed.q: A raster display with resolution 1024 × 768 and 8 bits per pixel needs a frame buffer of:
A 2-D rotation about the origin by angle θ maps (x, y) to:
o: (x cos θ − y sin θ, x sin θ + y cos θ)
(x cos θ + y sin θ, x sin θ − y cos θ)
fixed.w: The standard counter-clockwise rotation matrix is [cos θ −sin θ; sin θ cos θ].

fixed.q: Anti-aliasing is used to:
fixed.w: Aliasing comes from under-sampling; anti-aliasing smooths jaggies, e.g. by supersampling or area sampling.

fixed.q: The configuration file of an ASP.NET web application is:
fixed.w: web.config is an XML file holding settings such as connection strings, authentication and session state.

fixed.q: In a CRT, the property of phosphor that keeps it glowing after the beam moves is:
fixed.w: Persistence is the time a phosphor glows; low persistence needs a higher refresh rate to avoid flicker.

fixed.q: A random-scan (vector) display differs from raster scan because it:
o: Draws the picture line by line from a display file
Stores every pixel in a frame buffer
Is used for realistic shaded images
fixed.w: Random scan traces line segments directly (good for line drawings). Raster scan sweeps the whole screen row by row from a frame buffer.

fixed.q: Colour CRT monitors commonly use which technique?
fixed.w: Shadow-mask CRTs have three guns (R, G, B) and phosphor triads; beam penetration gave only a few colours.

fixed.q: Interlaced scanning displays:
o: Odd lines in one pass and even lines in the next
fixed.w: Interlacing reduces flicker at a lower refresh bandwidth by splitting a frame into two fields.

fixed.q: The ratio of the number of horizontal points to vertical points on a screen is the:
fixed.w: Aspect ratio (e.g. 4:3, 16:9). Resolution is the total number of points, e.g. 1920 × 1080.

fixed.q: JPEG compression is:
fixed.w: JPEG uses DCT-based lossy compression. PNG and GIF are lossless; GIF supports up to 256 colours.

fixed.q: MPEG is a family of standards for compressing:
fixed.w: MPEG-1, MPEG-2 (DVD), MPEG-4 (H.264); MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III.

fixed.q: The standard sampling rate of audio CDs is:
fixed.w: 44.1 kHz, more than twice the 20 kHz upper hearing limit (Nyquist).

fixed.q: MIDI files store:
o: Musical instructions (notes, instruments), not recorded sound
fixed.w: MIDI stores event messages for synthesisers, so files are very small.

fixed.q: Which image format is lossless and supports transparency?
fixed.w: PNG is lossless with an alpha channel.

fixed.q: Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) builds solids by:
o: Boolean operations (union, intersection, difference) on primitives
Listing every face, edge and vertex
Sweeping a 2-D shape along a path
fixed.w: CSG combines primitives with Boolean operations in a tree. B-rep stores faces, edges and vertices.

fixed.q: Boundary representation (B-rep) describes a solid by its:
fixed.w: B-rep stores the bounding surface topology and geometry.

fixed.q: Creating a solid by moving a 2-D shape along a path is a:
fixed.w: Translational and rotational sweeps make extrusions and solids of revolution.

fixed.q: For a simple convex polyhedron, Euler's formula is:
A B-spline curve differs from a Bezier curve because it offers:
o: Local control (moving a control point affects only part of the curve)
fixed.w: Moving one Bezier control point changes the whole curve; B-splines give local control.

fixed.q: An octree is used to represent:
o: 3-D objects by recursive subdivision of space into 8 octants
fixed.w: A quadtree subdivides 2-D space into 4 quadrants; an octree subdivides 3-D space into 8 octants.

theory.Computer graphics:
• Raster (pixels, frame buffer) vs vector (random scan). Frame buffer size = resolution × bits per pixel.
• Line: DDA (floating point) vs Bresenham (integer only). Circle: midpoint, 8-way symmetry.
• 2-D transformations with homogeneous coordinates (3×3): translation, rotation [cosθ −sinθ; sinθ cosθ], scaling, reflection, shear.
• Clipping: Cohen–Sutherland (4-bit outcodes), Liang–Barsky, Cyrus–Beck (lines); Sutherland–Hodgman, Weiler–Atherton (polygons).
• Hidden surface removal: Z-buffer (depth buffer), painter's algorithm, scan-line.
• Curves: Bezier (degree n has n+1 control points, passes through end points), B-spline (local control).
• Projection: parallel (orthographic, oblique) vs perspective (vanishing point).
• Colour: RGB (additive, screens), CMY/CMYK (subtractive, printers), HSV. Anti-aliasing removes jaggies.
theory..NET & ASP.NET:
• CLR: runtime (JIT, garbage collection, security). CTS: common types. CLS: rules for language interoperability. FCL/BCL: class library.
• Source → MSIL/CIL (+ metadata, in an assembly .dll/.exe) → JIT → native code. Shared assemblies are kept in the GAC.
• ASP.NET: web forms, page life cycle (Init, Load, events, Render, Unload), ViewState (hidden field), Session/Application state, web.config, Global.asax.
• ADO.NET: Connection, Command, DataReader (connected, forward-only), DataAdapter + DataSet (disconnected).
theory.Graphics hardware & display:
• CRT: electron gun, deflection, phosphor; persistence; refresh rate (≥ 60 Hz to avoid flicker); interlacing (odd/even fields).
• Raster scan (frame buffer of pixels, row by row) vs random/vector scan (display file of line commands, no jaggies).
• Colour CRT: shadow mask (RGB triads) or beam penetration (few colours). Flat panels: LCD, LED, plasma.
• Resolution, aspect ratio (4:3, 16:9), dot pitch. Frame buffer bits = width × height × bits per pixel.
• Input devices: tablet, light pen, joystick, data glove.
theory.Multimedia:
• Media: text, images, audio, video, animation.
• Images: JPEG (lossy, DCT), PNG (lossless, alpha), GIF (lossless, 256 colours, animation), BMP (uncompressed), TIFF.
• Audio: sampling (Nyquist ≥ 2 × highest frequency), CD 44.1 kHz 16-bit; WAV (uncompressed), MP3 (lossy), MIDI (instructions).
• Video: frame rate, MPEG-1/2/4, H.264; codecs.
• Authoring tools and hypermedia.
theory.Curves, surfaces & solid modelling:
• Bezier: degree n → n + 1 control points, passes through end points, global control, lies in convex hull. B-spline: local control. Hermite: end points + tangents.
• Surfaces: Bezier and B-spline patches; quadric surfaces (sphere, ellipsoid).
• Solid modelling: CSG (Boolean ops on primitives), B-rep (faces/edges/vertices), sweep (translational/rotational), octree (8 octants), spatial enumeration (voxels).
• Valid solid: complete, unambiguous. Euler: V − E + F = 2.
